problem: Assistive home robots typically rely on rigid, coordinate- or waypoint-based interfaces and struggle with natural language understanding, spatial reasoning (e.g. 'the chair near the sofa') and robust navigation.
motivation: About 16% of the world population has mobility impairments and depends on caregivers for daily tasks. A language-driven robot that grounds vague spatial commands in a semantic 3D map could give them more autonomy, and off-the-shelf pretrained models could make this practical.
key_idea: Use an LLM to extract the entities in a command, then find the target as the group of matching 3D object centroids (YOLO11-Seg + RTAB-Map + DBSCAN) with the smallest pairwise distance, and pass it as a goal to Nav2.
insight: The main insight is that the referent of a relational phrase ('chair near sofa') can be resolved by minimum pairwise distance among candidate centroids, so no VLN training is needed. Ablations are limited to component tests: YOLO11n-seg has the best speed/accuracy trade-off (Dice 0.94, 118.8 FPS), and DBSCAN/point-cloud filtering cut computation by 32.78% on average. Failures come from odometry loss and dense scenes with ambiguous spatial relations (9/12 success), so the pipeline is limited by perception and localization rather than by language parsing.
method: LLM parsing: GPT-4o-mini turns the command into a list of relevant entities (e.g. 'Go and take the pills on the table near the sofa' -> [sofa, table, pills]).
YOLO11-Seg segmentation: real-time instance segmentation of RGB frames from the RGB-D camera.
3D object positioning: masks are back-projected with depth into the camera frame, transformed to the map frame with RTAB-Map poses, and cross-checked with RTAB-Map's obstacle map to filter noise.
DBSCAN clustering: clusters the semantic point cloud into labeled 3D object centroids (epsilon and MinPts must be tuned).
Goal Search Algorithm: chooses the combination of context-object centroids with the minimum pairwise Euclidean distance as the goal area and sends it to Nav2.
Centroid update/persistence: after each goal, new centroids are matched within a spatial threshold to update stored positions; the list is saved and reloaded across sessions.
Simulation platform: TIAGo robot in ROS2 Gazebo (AWS RoboMaker small house world).

setting.backbone: GPT-4o-mini (frozen, API) + YOLO11n-seg (pretrained on COCO) + RTAB-Map + Nav2
setting.observation: RGB-D camera on TIAGo with RTAB-Map SLAM pose/map
setting.action_space: Nav2 goal poses (continuous navigation to 3D centroid goals)
setting.simulator: Gazebo (ROS2) with AWS RoboMaker small house world
setting.privileged: none (an initial exploration phase builds the map and centroid list; later trials reuse centroid lists from earlier runs)

numbers.eval_set_note: 4 trials x 3 commands = 12 tasks in the authors' own simulated house
numbers.method: Proposed VLN framework (YOLO11-Seg + RTAB-Map + DBSCAN + GPT-4o-mini + Nav2)
numbers.extra: Trial 1 used the centroid list from initial exploration; later trials reused updated lists from prior runs; not a standard benchmark
numbers.evidence: Overall, the integrated system achieved a 75% success rate (9 out of 12 tasks); Table V

numbers_note: No standard VLN benchmark. Component metrics: YOLOv11n Dice 0.94, IoU 0.91, 118.8 FPS; centroid labeling 100% (33 centroids); 70% of centroids correctly positioned; 2.1 s command-to-navigation latency; goal accuracy within 0.7 m claimed in abstract.
results: In a Gazebo house the system completed 9/12 relational-command tasks (75%), with Nav2 recovering from odometry-loss failures. YOLO11n-seg was the most balanced segmenter (Dice 0.94, 118.8 FPS), beating Mask R-CNN and Cascade R-CNN on speed at similar accuracy; the LLM parsed commands consistently.
limitations: Only simulation, a single house and a tiny test (12 tasks); no standard VLN benchmark or baseline comparison.
Failures from odometry drift near specific objects (e.g. refrigerator), ambiguous spatial relations in dense scenes, and only 70% correct centroid placement.
Needs an initial mapping phase, and cannot handle dynamic objects or object removal; minimum-pairwise-distance heuristic covers only simple 'near' relations.
